title.en: Exhaustive enumeration and the arithmetic identity of an adder

summary: Enumerate every input combination of a small combinational block and check its outputs against an independent table and the arithmetic identity.
objective: Every row satisfies the arithmetic identity and matches an independently written table, with no row sampled away.
applies_when: A combinational block has few enough inputs to enumerate completely.
Outputs have an arithmetic interpretation such as sum and carry.
The scene animates signal propagation between input change and output display.
intent_signals: check every input combination of this adder
the carry looks wrong for one case
example_prompts: Check this full adder against all eight input combinations.

principles: For a small combinational block exhaustive enumeration is cheap and complete, so sampling rows is unnecessary and misleading.

The arithmetic identity is the sharpest check for an adder: the weighted outputs must equal the number of true inputs on every row, which catches swapped sum and carry that per-gate inspection can miss.
The evaluator is the authority and the animation is a rendering of its result; the two are compared rather than one being trusted in place of the other.
implementation: Enumerate every input combination and record inputs, evaluator outputs and the arithmetic identity value for each row.
Compare outputs against an independently written table rather than against the same expression the scene evaluates.
Read displayed values from scene state for at least the rows where more than one output changes, so a display lag or animation-driven value is caught.
Treat the carry-in as a first-class input rather than a mode, and include the rows where only the carry-in changes.
observable_checks: On every row the sum bit plus twice the carry-out equals the number of true inputs; a failing row names the term to fix.
Evaluator outputs match the independent table on every row, with no row skipped as obvious.
Displayed outputs equal evaluator outputs once the transition completes, and any differing in-flight value is labelled as presentation rather than as a logic state.

known_limits: Checks Boolean function correctness only; no voltage, timing, hazard or transistor behaviour is covered.
Authored verification guidance; no circuit was evaluated or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: A full adder produces a two-bit result from three input bits, with the sum bit given by exclusive-or of the operands with the carry-in, and the carry-out either generated by the operands or propagated from the carry-in.
claims.scope: One-bit Boolean full adder as described in the cited section; no timing or device-level behaviour.
